label: Probability
overview: Probability measures how likely an event is, expressed as a fraction between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain). SAT questions involve basic probability (favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes), complementary events (P(not A) = 1 − P(A)), and conditional probability (probability given that something else is known). Two-way tables are a common data format.

keyFormulas.name: Independent events
keyFormulas.latex: P(A \text{ and } B) = P(A) \cdot P(B) \text{ (if independent)}

workedExamples.problem: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability it is NOT red?

commonMistakes.mistake: Using the full table total instead of the given row/column total for conditional probability
commonMistakes.fix: Conditional probability restricts the sample space to just the given condition. Use the row or column total for that condition as the denominator.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding probabilities for AND events instead of multiplying
commonMistakes.fix: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events. Only use addition for OR events: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).

quickTip: On two-way table probability questions, the denominator is almost always the key. Basic probability: use the grand total. Conditional probability: use the row or column total matching the given condition.
